title: on-call handoff draft - Oliver Wu
content:
Shift: 2026-03-03 08:00-16:00 PST (Oliver W.)
Summary: quick handoff notes for next oncall. Mostly quiet overnight but two items to watch. This is a working draft - TODOs marked.

ONGOING / RECENTLY RESOLVED:
- Rate-limiter alerts (low priority) - flaring between 03/02 22:00-03:00 UTC due to batch job surge. Autoscale handled, no customer impact reported. Root cause likely: nightly batch on analytics cluster overlapping with model warm-up. See ticket SRE-INC-2026-042.
  - Current mitigations: temporary throttle on analytics-job queue, increased worker pool for inference-pool-b.
  - Next steps: coordinate with infra to add jitter to batch start times (owner: Maya).

- Embeddings job failure (RESOLVED) - transient OOM on dedicated-host-7; restarted and added swap, monitoring for recurrence.

KNOWN ISSUES / WATCHLIST:
- KV cache compaction task sometimes spikes CPU on serving-runtime nodes. Watch cluster "serve-prod-1" during peak. If CPU > 85% for > 5m, temporarily shift traffic to serve-prod-2. Runbook snippet below.
- Legacy S3 path retention: some debug artifacts not cleaned; causes disk bloat on infra-snapshots. Ticket in backlog.

TEMP PROCEDURES / QUICK RUNBOOK (TEMP - DRAFT):
1) If rate-limiter alerts (pagerduty: SRE Rate Limit):
   - Check alert page: https://pagerduty.com/incidents (use service: Redwood - rate-limiter)
   - Run basic health: curl -sS https://health-api.prod.redwood.ai/health | jq .
   - Identify offending route: query logs in LogQL: `service=redwood-prod | json | route="/v1/generate" | top(10, request_id)` (adjust timeframe)
   - If autoscale not keeping up: increase pool for inference-pool-b (k8s scale): `kubectl scale deployment inference-pool-b --replicas=12 -n prod` (only if above 10 and after consulting oncall lead).
   - Post a short note in #sre-alerts and ping Maya Singh.

2) If KV cache compaction spike:
   - Check node metrics (Datadog): search tags `cluster:serve-prod-1` and `service:runtime` for CPU spike graphs.
   - If confirmed, run migration traffic: `route set serve-prod-1 -> serve-prod-2` via gateway console (ops-console -> traffic -> migrate).
   - If console not reachable, fallback: scale up serve-prod-2 by 2 replicas.

ESCALATION & CONTACTS:
- Primary oncall (this shift): Oliver Wu (pager: +1-555-0123, slack: @oliver.wu)
- Secondary: Maya Singh (pager: +1-555-0456, slack: @maya.singh)
- SRE lead: Ryan Patel (pager: +1-555-0789, slack: @ryan.patel)
- Infra eng: Priya Menon (slack: @priya.m)

MAINTENANCE / UPCOMING CHANGES:
- Planned: rolling upgrade for serve-prod-2 on 2026-03-07 02:00 UTC (low-traffic window). Might cause brief increased latency - tickets will be opened.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (draft):
- Add standard check for analytics batch window collisions into automatic oncall checks (owner: Maya).
- Flesh out exact thresholds for autoscale runbook (what to do at 70%, 80%, 90% CPU).
- Confirm whether dedicated-host-7 needs permanent memory increase or a better OOM killer config (owner: Ryan).

NOTES TO SELF (quick):
- When writing final runbook: move steps to numbered playbook entries, add screenshots for console steps, include exact Datadog dashboards.
- Keep this doc in users/ for iteration; once stable, promote to shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/runbooks/ (confluence link TODO).

RECENT LINKS / SEARCHES USED DURING SHIFT:
- Logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/goto?query=SRE-INC-2026-042
- Dashboards: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/serve-prod-overview
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-4287

END (draft)

----
Scratch notes (short):
- If anything spikes and no docs: set quick mitigation, then create ticket with title "hotfix: <short-desc> - <date>" and post in #ops-for-incident.
- Remind infra to add jitter: analytics-batch-cron -> cron-splay 120s.
